newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Coal Corp raises annual pre-tax profit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Coal Corp raises annual pre-tax profit.

text.p: State-owned Coal Corp of New Zealand Ltd announced on Thursday that it had made a pre-tax profit of NZ$27.85 million in the June year, 13.8 percent ahead of the previous year's.
A tax provision took the after-tax profit down to NZ$14.72 million from $17.44 million.
Revenue rose 4.7 percent to NZ$189.64 million.
Sales, in terms of tonnes per employee, rose 2.9 percent to 4,508 tonnes.
The result was built on sustained growth in the export business, which improved by 16 percent, and equated to total export sales of nearly 1.5 million tonnes.
Cost controls had a significant impact on the result, Chairman David Stock said in the annual report.
Stock said Coal Corp had produced strong earnings despite a sharp gain in the U.S. dollar, in which its exports are contracted.
Sales of coking cole, used primarily in the steel industry, grew by 10.4 percent while thermal coals, used mainly for electricity generation, grew by 40.8 percent, he said.
Exports to China doubled in the last year.

While sales in New Zealand were slightly lower, Stock expected a boost in the years to come as coal emerged as the logical energy source to fill a predicted shortfall in electricity supply early next century.
